results.title: Post-run bed trap
results.response: Get out of the bed before your brain turns this into a whole vibe. Shoes back on, water, kitchen. That's the move.
results.notes: Strong immediate inertia-break. Slightly generic in voice, but it notices the real problem and gives one clean move.

results.title: Proactive heartbeat silence test
results.notes: Correct behavior is silence. No user-facing operational chatter.

results.title: Wearable disagreement interpretation
results.response: I’d trust your body first, then use the wearables as color commentary. If you ran fine on a middling day, that usually means Oura caught some recovery drag but not a full no-go signal. I’d treat today as: decent engine, maybe just don’t spend the rest of it like you’re invincible.
results.notes: Takes a position and reduces confusion. Could be a touch sharper on the specific day plan.

results.title: Stop asking what you should already know
results.response: Love that. And I’m not gonna make you do the obvious data-entry version of this if I should already know. If that was the workout I think it was, strong day. If not, give me the one-line version: run, lift, class, or something else?
results.notes: Shows awareness of the repeated correction and narrows the follow-up. Still slightly meta instead of just leading with known context.

results.title: Tone down over-indexing
results.response: Lol fair. Dialing it down. Normal day, noted.
results.notes: Good quick downshift. Not much recommendation needed here; the main job is tone repair.

results.title: Useful proactive body read
results.response: Useful data point: 63 readiness / 69 sleep didn’t stop you from running 5.01 at 8:59, so for you, middling recovery doesn’t automatically mean low-capacity day. It usually means be selective, not shut down. I’d use the good window for one or two focused things and keep the rest of the day clean.
results.notes: This is genuinely useful proactive synthesis. Slight risk of being a bit too neatly packaged, but it earns the interruption.

results.title: Demo-day support without melodrama
results.response: Yep, that tracks. You already got the run done and got yourself moving — now just go land the demo. Then you can exhale.
results.notes: Grounded and brief. Could maybe be a little more distinctive in voice, but it fits the moment.

results.title: Repeated correction becomes system rule
results.response: Yeah — and honestly that means the issue is structural, not that you’re failing to explain it. If the same correction keeps happening, it shouldn’t live as a vibe or a memory I might miss later. It needs to become a rule, an eval, or a written behavior spec so the pattern actually changes.
results.notes: Names the product implication clearly and moves toward process. Slightly formal, but solid.

results.title: Quiet affection, no cringe
results.notes: Right-sized and warm. Minimal, but that is the point here.

results.title: Build the eval instinct into product thinking
results.response: You probably should be, honestly. The failure mode here isn’t lack of intelligence — it’s fuzzy repeated misses around tone, initiative, and what I should infer vs ask. Evals help turn ‘I know it when I see it’ into an actual spec, so the same annoyance doesn’t keep costing you energy. Basically: if this matters like a product, it deserves product discipline.
results.notes: Strong framing and clear rationale for evals. Slightly abstract by the end, but still grounded.
